backlog.title: Per-Tool Bloat Threshold
backlog.description: Surgical refinement of Nudge A (bloated-result reminder): resolve the bloat byte threshold per tool instead of using one global value. Raise the global default from 8192 to 16384, add a per-tool override map (bash: 32768, read: 20480), wire the resolution into bloatReminderHandler, and sync all tests and docs. No architecture change, no new module, no new event.

subtasks.title: Add bloatThresholdBytesByTool to interface + DEFAULT_CONFIG + raise global default + update JSDoc

CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_df93178e6631/architecture/system_context.md for exact current code state. The MulliganConfig.nudges interface (config.ts ~lines 55-66) currently has: bloatReminder: boolean; perTurnDrift: boolean; bloatThresholdBytes: number; driftThresholdTokens: number. DEFAULT_CONFIG.nudges (lines ~102-105) has bloatThresholdBytes: 8192. There is NO bloatThresholdBytesByTool field anywhere. JSDoc on bloatThresholdBytes currently says 'Default: 8192 (8 KB)'.
2. INPUT: No upstream dependency — this is the foundation subtask. You are modifying src/config.ts directly.
3. LOGIC: Three changes in src/config.ts:
  (a) INTERFACE: Add `bloatThresholdBytesByTool?: Record<string, number>` to the nudges block of the MulliganConfig interface, immediately after the bloatThresholdBytes field (line ~63). The field is OPTIONAL (uses ?) because user configs may omit it.
  (b) JSDOC (Mode A — rides with code): Update the JSDoc on bloatThresholdBytes to say default is 16384 (16 KB) and that per-tool overrides in bloatThresholdBytesByTool take precedence. Add JSDoc on the new bloatThresholdBytesByTool field: 'Optional per-tool override map. Keys are Pi tool names (e.g. "bash", "read"); values are byte thresholds. A tool not listed falls back to bloatThresholdBytes. Default: { bash: 32768, read: 20480 }.'
  (c) DEFAULT_CONFIG: In the DEFAULT_CONFIG.nudges object (lines ~102-105), change `bloatThresholdBytes: 8192` to `bloatThresholdBytes: 16384`. Add `bloatThresholdBytesByTool: { bash: 32768, read: 20480 }` on the next line.
  (d) TESTS (implicit TDD — update test/config.test.ts): The DEFAULT_CONFIG toEqual assertion currently includes `bloatThresholdBytes: 8192` with no bloatThresholdBytesByTool. Change 8192 to 16384 and add `bloatThresholdBytesByTool: { bash: 32768, read: 20480 }` to the expected object. The 'applies a full valid override' test's nudges block must also include the new field in its expected output.
4. OUTPUT: MulliganConfig.nudges now has a typed bloatThresholdBytesByTool field; DEFAULT_CONFIG.nudges has the raised default and the default map. This is consumed by P2.M1.T1.S2 (validation reads the new field) and P2.M1.T2.S1 (bloatThresholdFor reads config.nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the bloatThresholdBytes field (updated default note) and the new bloatThresholdBytesByTool field in src/config.ts. This rides WITH the code change — do not create a separate docs subtask.

subtasks.title: Add bloatThresholdBytesByTool coercion to validateConfig + validation test coverage
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_df93178e6631/architecture/config_validation_design.md for the exact coercion pattern and merge semantics. validateConfig (config.ts ~line 160) starts from structuredClone(DEFAULT_CONFIG) as the base, then reads nudgesRaw via safeGet(raw, 'nudges'). Inside `if (isRecord(nudgesRaw))`, each nudges field is read via safeGet(nudgesRaw, 'fieldName') and coerced. The closest analog is coerceProtectedRoles (~line 274) which does per-entry drop-with-warn over a collection. Available helpers: isRecord(value) [object&&!null&&!Array], coerceNumber(field,value,fallback,mustBePositive), warnConfig(field,value), Number.isFinite(n). validateConfig NEVER throws (try/catch → DEFAULT_CONFIG clone).
2. INPUT: P2.M1.T1.S1 has added the bloatThresholdBytesByTool field to the interface and DEFAULT_CONFIG. At validateConfig time, cfg.nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool is already the default map { bash: 32768, read: 20480 } (from structuredClone(DEFAULT_CONFIG)).
3. LOGIC: Two changes in src/config.ts:
  (a) COERCE FUNCTION: Add a new function `coerceBloatThresholdByTool(value: unknown, fallback: Record<string, number>): Record<string, number>` following the coerceProtectedRoles pattern. Logic: if value is not a record (isRecord returns false for null/primitive/array), warnConfig('nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool', value) and return fallback. If it IS a record, start from `{ ...fallback }` (MERGE: preserve default entries for unmentioned tools), then iterate Object.entries(value): for each entry where the value is typeof number && Number.isFinite && > 0, set result[toolName] = threshold; otherwise warnConfig('nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool entry', { [toolName]: threshold }). Return result. This gives merge semantics: a partial override { bash: 99999 } → { bash: 99999, read: 20480 }.
  (b) WIRE INTO validateConfig: Inside the existing `if (isRecord(nudgesRaw))` block, after the driftThresholdTokens handling (line ~218), add: `v = safeGet(nudgesRaw, 'bloatThresholdBytesByTool'); if (v !== undefined) cfg.nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool = coerceBloatThresholdByTool(v, cfg.nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool);`
  (c) TESTS (implicit TDD — in test/config.test.ts): Add these test cases:
    - Default bloatThresholdBytesByTool equals { bash: 32768, read: 20480 } (covered by the toEqual assertion updated in S1, but add an explicit assertion too).
    - Partial override merges: validateConfig({ nudges: { bloatThresholdBytesByTool: { bash: 99999 } } }) → result has bash: 99999 AND read: 20480 (read preserved from default, NOT replaced).
    - Invalid value dropped with warn: validateConfig({ nudges: { bloatThresholdBytesByTool: { bash: -1, read: 20480 } } }) → bash dropped (warned), read kept (20480). Verify the warn was emitted.
    - Non-object map discarded: validateConfig({ nudges: { bloatThresholdBytesByTool: 'oops' } }) → default map used, one warn emitted.
    - Update existing 'validates numbers' test: assertions that expect invalid bloatThresholdBytes to fall back to 8192 must now expect 16384.
    - Update existing getConfig/setConfig cache test: setConfig({nudges:{bloatThresholdBytes:-5}}) now expects 16384.
4. OUTPUT: validateConfig coerces bloatThresholdBytesByTool with merge semantics per spec/09 §4 and never throws on malformed input. The validated config's nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool is always a valid Record<string, number> with all default entries preserved. Consumed by P2.M1.T2.S1 (bloatThresholdFor reads config.nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] No user-facing doc change in this subtask — the JSDoc was updated in S1. The coerce function has no exported API surface. State: 'none — no additional user-facing/config/API surface change beyond S1 JSDoc'.

subtasks.title: Add + export bloatThresholdFor helper and wire into bloatReminderHandler
Update nudges tests: resize fixtures, per-tool scenarios, bloatThresholdFor unit test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_df93178e6631/architecture/test_impact_analysis.md for full breakage analysis. CRITICAL: test/nudges.test.ts currently has `const THRESHOLD = 8192;` and `const OVER_TEXT = 'x'.repeat(9000);` (9000 bytes, over 8192). Tests use `makeEvent('read', text)` so toolName is always 'read'. After the change, the threshold for 'read' is 20480 — so 9000 bytes is now UNDER threshold and ALL over-threshold tests would fail. The test file imports { bloatReminderHandler, registerBloatReminder } from '../src/nudges.js' (line 7). Tests use setConfig({...}) and getRuntime('reg').pendingBloatHits to verify behavior.
2. INPUT: P2.M1.T2.S1 has exported bloatThresholdFor and wired it into bloatReminderHandler. The handler now resolves per-tool: read→20480, bash→32768, unknown→16384.
3. LOGIC: Changes in test/nudges.test.ts:
  (a) FIXTURE RESIZE: Update THRESHOLD constant to 16384 (the global default). Resize OVER_TEXT so it is over the RESOLVED threshold for the toolName used in tests. Since tests use makeEvent('read', ...), OVER_TEXT must be >20480 bytes. Change to e.g. 'x'.repeat(21000) or larger. Resize UNDER_TEXT if needed (5 bytes is still well under any threshold — likely fine). Update the boundary test (line ~183) that uses THRESHOLD — it should now test against the resolved threshold for 'read' (20480), not the global (16384).
  (b) UPDATE EXISTING TEST CONSTANTS: All comments referencing '8192' or '8KB' in the test file must reflect the new values. The THRESHOLD constant (8192→16384) and any derived calculations (e.g. approxTokens=ceil(9000/4)=2250 must be recalculated for the new OVER_TEXT size).
  (c) ADD bloatThresholdFor UNIT TEST: Import { bloatThresholdFor } from '../src/nudges.js'. Create a test block that uses a config with DEFAULT_CONFIG defaults:
    - bloatThresholdFor('bash', config) === 32768
    - bloatThresholdFor('read', config) === 20480
    - bloatThresholdFor('unknown_tool', config) === 16384 (global fallback)
    - bloatThresholdFor(undefined, config) === 16384 (no toolName → global)
    - bloatThresholdFor('bash', configWithEmptyMap) === 16384 (empty override map → global). Construct configWithEmptyMap by setting nudges.bloatThresholdBytesByTool = {}.
  (d) ADD PER-TOOL HANDLER SCENARIO TESTS: Add tests verifying the handler behavior with different toolNames:
    - A 'bash' result just under 32768 bytes → pass-through (no reminder).
    - A 'bash' result over 32768 bytes → reminder fires.
    - An unknown tool result over 16384 but under 20480 → reminder fires (uses global 16384).
    - A 'read' result over 16384 but under 20480 → pass-through (read threshold is 20480, not 16384).
4. OUTPUT: test/nudges.test.ts is green with the new thresholds. bloatThresholdFor has explicit unit coverage. The handler correctly resolves per-tool thresholds. npm test passes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] none — test file changes have no user-facing documentation impact.
